15 A solid sphere, which is less dense than water, is held completely immersed in water a few
metres below the surface. The density of the water is uniform.
The sphere is released. Immediately after release, the sphere rises.
Which row describes the changes in the magnitudes of the upthrust on the sphere and the
resultant force on the sphere as it rises?
resultant force
upthrust on
the sphere
on the sphere
A
constant
decreasing
B
constant
increasing
C
decreasing
decreasing
D
decreasing
increasing

hints: Notice the sphere is held completely immersed a few metres below the surface, so check whether displaced volume changes while it is still rising underwater.
Connect displaced volume to Archimedes principle $U = \rho V g$ with uniform water density $\rho$ and constant sphere volume $V$.
Connect the speed of the rising sphere to viscous drag opposing motion and to resultant force $F = U - W - D$ with constant weight $W$.
walkthrough: List the vertical forces after release: weight $W = \rho_{sphere}Vg$ downward and constant, upthrust $U$ upward, and drag $D$ opposing motion.
Use Archimedes principle: $U$ equals weight of displaced water, $U = \rho_{water}V_{submerged}g$.
While the sphere is still completely below the surface, $V_{submerged}$ equals the full sphere volume $V$ and $\rho_{water}$ is uniform, so $U$ is constant.
Immediately after release speed is near zero so $D$ is near zero, giving an upward resultant $F = U - W$ because $\rho_{sphere} < \rho_{water}$.
As the sphere rises and speeds up, downward drag $D$ increases, so $F = U - W - D$ with constant $U - W$ must decrease in magnitude.
Constant upthrust with decreasing resultant matches the row with constant then decreasing. This is option A

A.explanation: Upthrust stays constant while fully immersed and resultant $U - W - D$ falls as drag $D$ grows with speed.

B.explanation: Upthrust is constant but resultant cannot increase because growing downward drag reduces the net upward force.

C.explanation: Upthrust does not decrease while the sphere is still completely immersed in water of uniform density.

D.explanation: Upthrust does not decrease when fully submerged and resultant does not increase as drag opposes the rising motion.
